bull.b: Sharp TTM growth and high margins show strong demand, favorable mix and operating leverage. This strengthens internal funding for technology transitions, although memory pricing can still normalize across the cycle.

Large operating and free cash flow provides capacity to fund fabs, R&D and shareholder returns while preserving resilience. The balance-sheet context further supports flexibility, but historical cycle volatility means cash conversion is not assured.

SCAs and RPOs create contractual volume visibility with major customers and support capacity planning for AI-related memory demand. Broader coverage could reduce spot-market exposure, though pricing terms remain important.

bear.b: Memory profitability has historically swung from deep losses to exceptionally high margins, showing exposure to ASPs, utilization and product mix. Pricing or demand normalization could materially reduce earnings and cash generation.

Planned CapEx and rising OpEx increase fixed costs and execution risk. Returns depend on timely fab, packaging and technology ramps, while delays, weaker demand or overspending could pressure free cash flow.

Long-lived shortages involving fabs, skilled workers, permitting and energy infrastructure can constrain shipment growth and delay customer fulfillment. Addressing the bottlenecks requires substantial capital and sustained execution.
